title: Configure WLAN using WLC GUI with WPA2 PSK

questions.question: After configuring a WLAN, your users complain that they do not see the SSID. What could be wrong?
choices: Radio Policy is configured to all.

correct.explanation: If the WLAN status is disabled (admin down), clients will not see or join the SSID regardless of other settings.

incorrect.explanation: SSID beaconing enabled is required for visibility — this choice says it is already enabled, so it is not the problem described.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Picking a healthy setting as the fault
incorrect.whatItDoes: SSID beaconing is enabled. describes a mechanism that could sound plausible for wlc gui wlan.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: Given wlc gui wlan, Status is disabled. matches the tested behavior — SSID beaconing is enabled. applies a different mechanism.

incorrect.explanation: Multicast settings affect delivery of multicast traffic — they do not typically hide the SSID from clients.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Multicast support is disabled. describes a mechanism that could sound plausible for wlc gui wlan.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: Given wlc gui wlan, Status is disabled. matches the tested behavior — Multicast support is disabled. applies a different mechanism.

incorrect.explanation: Radio policy set to all bands should still advertise the SSID — disabled WLAN status is the direct block.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Over-focusing on band policy when the WLAN is admin-down
incorrect.whatItDoes: Radio Policy is configured to all. describes a mechanism that could sound plausible for wlc gui wlan.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: Given wlc gui wlan, Status is disabled. matches the tested behavior — Radio Policy is configured to all. applies a different mechanism.

answerReview.examTip: SSID not visible → check WLAN enabled status first, then beacon/hide SSID settings.

questions.question: How many pre-shared keys can be configured for a specific WPA2 WLAN?
choices: One PSK (one hex or one ASCII)
Two PSKs (one hex and one ASCII)
Four PSKs (two hex and two ASCII)

correct.explanation: A WPA2-Personal WLAN uses one PSK at a time — either hex or ASCII format, not multiple concurrent keys.

incorrect.explanation: Cisco WLC WPA2-Personal does not provision separate hex and ASCII PSKs simultaneously — one active key only.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Assuming dual hex+ASCII keys on one WLAN
incorrect.whatItDoes: Two PSKs (one hex and one ASCII) describes a mechanism that could sound plausible for wlc gui wlan.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: Given wlc gui wlan, One PSK (one hex or one ASCII) matches the tested behavior — Two PSKs (one hex and one ASCII) applies a different mechanism.

incorrect.explanation: There is not a pool of four PSKs per WLAN — personal mode is one shared key for all clients.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Expecting multiple rotating PSK slots like enterprise policies
incorrect.whatItDoes: Four PSKs (two hex and two ASCII) describes a mechanism that could sound plausible for wlc gui wlan.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: Given wlc gui wlan, One PSK (one hex or one ASCII) matches the tested behavior — Four PSKs (two hex and two ASCII) applies a different mechanism.

incorrect.explanation: PSK count is limited by design — not unlimited keys on a single WPA2-Personal SSID.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Treating PSK like per-user enterprise credentials
incorrect.whatItDoes: Unlimited number of PSKs describes a mechanism that could sound plausible for wlc gui wlan.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: Given wlc gui wlan, One PSK (one hex or one ASCII) matches the tested behavior — Unlimited number of PSKs applies a different mechanism.

answerReview.examTip: WPA2-Personal = one PSK (hex OR ASCII). Enterprise = per-user via RADIUS.

questions.question: You are configuring a WPA2 WLAN. Which security configuration should you use for the highest level of security?

correct.explanation: WPA2 with AES (CCMP) is the strongest common WPA2 cipher — avoid TKIP/RC4 legacy options.

incorrect.explanation: WPA-AES is first-generation WPA — WPA2-AES is the stronger, current standard for new deployments.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Stopping at WPA instead of WPA2
incorrect.whatItDoes: WPA-AES describes a mechanism that could sound plausible for wlc gui wlan.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: Given wlc gui wlan, WPA2-AES matches the tested behavior — WPA-AES applies a different mechanism.

incorrect.explanation: WPA2-TKIP keeps legacy cipher support — AES/CCMP is stronger and preferred for highest security.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Choosing TKIP under a WPA2 SSID for "security"
incorrect.whatItDoes: WPA2-TKIP describes a mechanism that could sound plausible for wlc gui wlan.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: Given wlc gui wlan, WPA2-AES matches the tested behavior — WPA2-TKIP applies a different mechanism.

incorrect.explanation: RC4-based options are legacy — WPA2-AES (CCMP) is the exam answer for strongest WPA2 cipher.
incorrect.whatItDoes: WPA2-RC4 describes a mechanism that could sound plausible for wlc gui wlan.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: Given wlc gui wlan, WPA2-AES matches the tested behavior — WPA2-RC4 applies a different mechanism.

answerReview.examTip: Highest WPA2 security → WPA2-AES (CCMP). Disable TKIP when hardening.

questions.question: You are setting up a wireless network for a client. Their requirements are to minimize the infrastructure and support the highest security. Which wireless encryption standard should be configured to satisfy the requirements?

correct.explanation: WPA2-Personal (PSK) minimizes infrastructure — no RADIUS — while still using modern WPA2 security for a small site.

incorrect.explanation: WPA-Enterprise requires RADIUS and more infrastructure — opposite of minimizing backend services.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Choosing enterprise auth when minimal infra is required
incorrect.whatItDoes: WPA-Enterprise describes a mechanism that could sound plausible for wlc gui wlan.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: Given wlc gui wlan, WPA2-Personal matches the tested behavior — WPA-Enterprise applies a different mechanism.

incorrect.explanation: WPA3-Enterprise also needs RADIUS and newer hardware — more complex than WPA2-Personal for a minimal setup.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Over-engineering with WPA3-Enterprise for minimal infra
incorrect.whatItDoes: WPA3-Enterprise describes a mechanism that could sound plausible for wlc gui wlan.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: Given wlc gui wlan, WPA2-Personal matches the tested behavior — WPA3-Enterprise applies a different mechanism.

incorrect.explanation: Original WPA-Personal is older than WPA2-Personal — the stem asks for modern security with minimal infrastructure.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Reverting to WPA instead of WPA2-Personal
incorrect.whatItDoes: WPA-Personal describes a mechanism that could sound plausible for wlc gui wlan.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: Given wlc gui wlan, WPA2-Personal matches the tested behavior — WPA-Personal applies a different mechanism.

answerReview.examTip: Small site, minimal infra, shared key OK → WPA2-Personal. Enterprise/users → WPA2-Enterprise + RADIUS.
